evidence.description: Task { await self.retrieveStoredCredentials() } is called inside the public init.

candidates.explanation: The initializer contains a Task that starts an asynchronous operation (retrieveStoredCredentials) without any mechanism to handle the result or manage the lifecycle of the task. This can lead to race conditions where the user profile or login state is updated unpredictably during the initialization phase of the actor.
candidates.title: Unstructured Task in Initializer

evidence.description: Task { await dispatchAuthStateChange(...) } is used inside setupTokensWithCredentials.

candidates.explanation: The `setupTokensWithCredentials` method launches an unstructured Task to dispatch state changes. Since this is an actor, launching a Task to call another method on the same actor (dispatchAuthStateChange) can lead to out-of-order execution of state updates if multiple setup calls occur in rapid succession.
candidates.title: Unstructured Task for State Dispatch

evidence.description: Task { @MainActor in NotificationCenter.default.post(...) } inside userProfile didSet.

candidates.explanation: The `userProfile` property uses a `didSet` observer that spawns a new Task to post a notification on the `@MainActor`. This creates a detached execution flow where the notification might be posted at an unpredictable time relative to other state changes, potentially leading to inconsistent UI updates.
candidates.title: Unstructured Task in Property Observer

evidence.description: The login function executes multiple awaits without tracking or cancelling previous tasks.

candidates.explanation: The `login` method performs multiple asynchronous operations (startAuth, storeCredentials, fetchUserInfoFromAuth0) sequentially. If a request fails or takes a long time, there is no mechanism provided to cancel the previous request if a new login attempt is initiated, which can lead to 'last-request-wins' race conditions.
candidates.title: Lack of Task Cancellation in Login Flow
